# children

#### Course: JavaScript in Browser

## children

To access all children of an element, you use the children property.

![children](data:image/png;base64,)

Let's log the children using this property:

```html
1<div class="container">
2    <h1>Price List</h1>
3    <ul id="price-list">
4        <li class="item">Milk <span>$2.50</span></li>
5        <li class="item">Bread <span>$1.50</span></li>
6        <li class="item">Toothpaste <span>$3.00</span></li>
7    </ul>
8    <button id="update">Update First Item</button>
9</div>
```

```css
1* {
2    margin: 0;

4    box-sizing: border-box;
5}
6
7body {
8    font-family: Arial, sans-serif;

22}
23
```

```javascript
1const priceList = document.querySelector("#price-list");
2const update = document.querySelector("#update")
3
4update.addEventListener("click", () => {
5    // Logs all children of price-list
6    console.log(priceList.children)
7});
```

Click the Update First Item button.

Right now, it logs all children of price-list in an array-like object, called HTMLCollection.
